decision_conditions:
Condition : 1 - The development hereby permitted shall begin not later than three years from the date of this decision.
Reason: In order to comply with Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, as amended by Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.
Condition : 2 - The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans and specifications: 25.04.002, 2024-10-200, 25106-T, 2450-KC-XX-YTREE-TCP01Rev0, Tree Survey April 2025 Received 15 December 2025
Archaeological Desk-Based Assessment February 2026, Heritage Statement March 2026 Received 11 March 2026
Acoustic Assessment Revision C March 2026, Acoustics Technical Note March 2026, Flood Risk Assessment and Surface Water Drainage Strategy AEG8224_TW8_Syon Park_01, Drainage Strategy (Addendum to FRA ref AEG8224_TW8_Syon Park_01), Ecological Impact Assessment Land at Syon Park April 2026, BNG Metric, BNG Condition Assessment Sheet Baseline Habitat Map, Post Development Habitat Map, Syon Park Outdoor LED Padel Tennis Lighting Design, Padel Shift Operational Noise Management Plan, Syon House Padel Courts � Flood Defence Structural Survey 22 April 2026 Received 23 April 2026
25.04_100 Rev P02, 25.04_101 Rev P02, 25.04_200 Rev P02, 25.04_205 Rev P02, 25.04_210 Rev P02 Received 27 April 2026
25.04_001 Rev P03 Received 19 May 2026 
Transport Statement Revision C Received 08 June 2026  .
Reason: In order to ensure the development is carried out in accordance with the planning permission.
Condition : 3 - Customers shall only be permitted onsite between the following hours:
�	Monday to Friday: 07:00 to 22:00
�	Saturday: 08:00 to 21:00
�	Sunday and Public/Bank Holidays: 08:00 to 21:00
Reason: In order to protect neighbours' living conditions. 
Note:  If this approved use requires a trading licence from the Council (for example, because you intend to sell alcohol or offer entertainment) you should obtain this before you start to trade and note that the Licensing Panel will enquire about and wish you to disclose the terms of this permission and will likely align the terms of the licence with those set out here.  If your licence application seeks to exceed these hours, you will first need to have sought and obtained formally a variation to this condition by making a planning application.
Condition : 4 - The use of indoor padel courts hereby permitted shall not be carried on outside the following times: 
�	Monday to Friday: 07:00 to 22:00
�	Saturday: 08:00 to 21:00
�	Sunday and Public/Bank Holidays: 08:00 to 21:00
Reason: To protect the living conditions of neighbouring residents
Condition : 5 - The use of outdoor padel courts hereby permitted shall not be carried on outside the following times: 
�	Monday to Friday: 08:00 to 21:00
�	Saturday: 09:00 to 20:00
�	Sunday and Public/Bank Holidays: 09:00 to 20:00
Reason: To protect the living conditions of neighbouring residents.  
Condition : 6 - The floodlighting on the outdoor courts hereby permitted shall only be operated between:
�	Monday to Friday: 08:00 to 21:00
�	Saturday: 09:00 to 20:00
�	Sunday and Public/Bank Holidays: 09:00 to 20:00
Reason: In order to protect neighbours' living conditions and the character of the locality
Condition : 7 - External artificial lighting at the development site shall not exceed lux levels of vertical illumination at neighbouring premises that are recommended by the Institution of Lighting Professionals in the 'Guidance Note 01/21: Guidance Notes for the Reduction of Obtrusive Light'. Lighting should be minimised, and glare and sky glow should be prevented by correctly using, locating, aiming, and shielding luminaires, in accordance with Guidance Notes.
Reason: To ensure that the amenity of occupiers of surrounding premises is not adversely affected by lighting.   
Condition : 8 - The development hereby permitted shall be implemented in strict accordance with the approved Padel Shift Operational Noise Management Plan Received 23 April 2026. 
Reason: In order to protect residential occupiers from noise and disturbance.
Condition : 9 - The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the recommendations of the approved Ecological Impact Assessment Land at Syon Park April 2026 Received 23 April 2026.
Reason: In the interests of nature conservation.
Condition : 10 - No development shall take place until a Construction Logistics Plan (CLP), written in accordance with current TfL guidance, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The CLP shall include: [delete or add items as necessary]
(a)	a site plan (showing the elements set out below);
(b)	confirmation that a pre-start record of site conditions on the adjoining public highway will be undertaken with Hounslow Highways and a commitment to repair any damage caused;
(c)	provision for the parking of vehicles of site operatives and visitors;
(d)	provisions for loading, unloading and storage of plant and materials within the site;
(e)	details of access to the site, including means to control and manage access and egress of vehicles to and from the site for the duration of construction including phasing arrangements;
(f)	details of vehicle routeing from the site to the wider strategic road network;
(g)	the erection and maintenance of security hoarding including decorative displays and facilities for public viewing, where appropriate;
(h)	provision of wheel washing facilities at the site exit and a commitment to sweep adjacent roads when required and at the request of the Council;
(i)	a scheme for recycling/disposing of waste resulting from demolition and construction works; 
(j)	measures to ensure the safety of all users of the public highway especially cyclists and pedestrians in the vicinity of the site and especially at the access;
(k)	commitment to liaise with other contractors in the vicinity of the site to maximise the potential for consolidation and to minimise traffic impacts;
(l)	no deliveries before 9.30am and after 3pm to avoid school opening and closing times and peak hours, unless otherwise agreed in advance with the council and details of a booking system to avoid vehicles waiting on the public highway;
(m)	all necessary traffic orders and other permissions required to allow safe access to the site to be secured and imp
Condition : 11 - Notwithstanding any details included in the submitted plans, no development above ground level (except any demolition, site clearance, ground investigation and remediation work) shall take place until details of both hard and soft landscape works have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, in consultation with the Canal and Rivers Trust. These details shall include: 
(a) a statement setting out the design objectives and how these will be delivered; 
(b) existing and proposed finished levels or contours; 
(c) means of enclosure/boundary treatment(s) and retaining structures;
(d) vehicle and pedestrian access and circulation areas;
(e) hard surfacing materials; 
(f) minor artefacts and structures (e.g. furniture, play equipment, refuse or other storage units, signs, lighting, CCTV etc.); 
(g) proposed and existing functional services above and below ground (e.g. drainage, power, communications cables, pipelines etc. indicating alignments, levels, access points, supports as relevant);  
(h) planting plans, written specifications (including cultivation and other operations associated with plant and grass establishment); schedules of plants, noting species, plant sizes and proposed numbers and densities where appropriate; and
(i) an implementation programme (including phasing of work where relevant).
The landscaping works shall comply with the requirements specified in BS 3936 (1992) 'Specification of Nursery Stock Part 1 Trees and Shrubs', and in BS 4428 (1989) 'Recommendations for General Landscape Operations', and shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details before the development hereby permitted is first occupied or brought into use, or such other date(s) as may be specified in the agreed implementation programme.
Reason: In order to ensure a satisfactory appearance of the site and the area and to promote biodiversity.
Condition : 12 - The trees that are specified on the drawings hereby approved to be retained shall be protected before commencement of any works on site and throughout the course of the development by methods that conform to the best practice guidance contained in British Standard BS5837: 2012 or any guidance that shall have superseded it

Reason: In order to ensure a satisfactory appearance of the site and the area and to promote biodiversity.
Condition : 13 - Notwithstanding any details included in the submitted plans, before above ground works commence, an ecological lighting plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, in consultation with the Canal and Rivers Trust. The plan should follow The Bat Conservation Trust's guidance and include:
�	Technical description, design, or specification of external lighting to be installed including shields, cowls, or blinds where appropriate. 
�	A description of the luminosity of lights and their light colour. 
�	The location and where appropriate the elevation and height of the light fixings. 
�	Methods to control lighting; and 
The development shall be maintained thereafter in accordance with these details. 
Reason: In order to ensure a satisfactory appearance of the site and the area and to promote biodiversity.
Condition : 14 - No development shall take place, including any works of demolition, until an Ecological Management Plan has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the local planning authority. The Plan shall include:
(i)	measures to prevent any runoff and pollution (from dust and debris) from harming nearby water way(s) during construction; nationally recognised best practice construction methods for the purpose shall be specified to achieve this.
(ii)	Details of lighting during construction 
(iii)	Details of materials storage and waste management 
The approved Plan shall be adhered to throughout the construction period.
Reason: In order to ensure the protection of wildlife and supporting habitat and secure opportunities for the enhancement of the nature conservation value of the site.
Condition : 15 - Prior to the first commencement of the hereby approved development, a Biodiversity Gain Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, the Plan shall include;
(a) information about the steps taken or to be taken to minimise the adverse effect of the development on the biodiversity of the onsite habitat and any other habitat,
(b) the pre-development biodiversity value of the onsite habitat,
(c) the post-development biodiversity value of the onsite habitat,
(d) any registered offsite biodiversity gain allocated to the development and the biodiversity value of that gain in relation to the development,
(e) any biodiversity credits purchased for the development, and
(f) such other matters as the Secretary of State may by regulations specify.
The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approved Plan prior to the first occupation of the development. Any habitats created or enhanced on-site and off-site in accordance with the Biodiversity Gain Plan must be maintained thereafter for a minimum of 30 years.
Reason. In the interests of improving Biodiversity and in accordance with The Town and Country Planning Act 1990, Section 90A, Schedule 7A.
Condition : 16 - A) Prior to the first commencement of the hereby approved development a Habitat Management and Monitoring Plan (HMMP) prepared in accordance with the approved Biodiversity Gain Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Plan shall include:
(i) a non-technical summary;
(ii) the roles and responsibilities of the people or organisation(s) delivering the HMMP
(iii) the planned habitat creation and enhancement works to create or improve habitat to achieve the biodiversity net gain in accordance with the approved Biodiversity Gain Plan;
(iv) the management measures to maintain habitat in accordance with the approved Biodiversity Gain Plan for a period of 30 years from the completion of development; and 
(v) the monitoring methodology and frequency in respect of the created or enhanced habitat to be submitted to the local planning authority. 

B) No occupation or use of the hereby approved development shall take place until:
(i) the habitat creation and enhancement works set out in the approved HMMP have been completed; and 
(ii) a completion report, evidencing the completed habitat enhancements, has been submitted to, and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. 
The created and/or enhanced habitat specified in the approved HMMP shall be managed and maintained in accordance with the approved HMMP.

C) Monitoring reports shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority in writing in accordance with the methodology and frequency specified in the approved HMMP.

Reason. In the interests of improving Biodiversity and in accordance with The Town and Country Planning Act 1990, Section 90A, Schedule 7A.
Condition : 17 - Prior to commencement of groundworks (excluding site investigations and demolition), the applicant shall have submitted to the local planning authority for approval in writing a final detailed drainage design, including drawings and supporting calculations, aligned with the Drainage Strategy (Addendum to FRA ref AEG8224_TW8_Syon Park_01) Received 23 April 2026 and associated material hereby approved. A detailed management plan confirming routine maintenance tasks for all drainage components shall also be submitted and approved which demonstrates how the drainage system is to be maintained for the lifetime of the development. The development shall be carried out in strict compliance with the approved details.
Reason: In order to prevent the risk of flooding to and from the site.
Condition : 18 - No part of the development hereby approved shall be occupied until evidence (photographs and copies of installation contracts, along with a written confirmation) has been submitted to the local planning authority and approved in writing to demonstrate that the sustainable drainage scheme hereby approved has been completed in accordance with the submitted final detailed drainage designs. The sustainable drainage scheme shall be managed and maintained thereafter in accordance with the agreed management and maintenance plan for all of the proposed drainage components.
Reason: In order to ensure that the methods to mitigate the risk of surface water flooding have been implemented as agreed and that the drainage system is suitably managed.
Condition : 19 - The development shall not be occupied until details of lighting to be installed along the Capital Ring Road towards Snakes and Ladders, extending to the proposed site have been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: In order to ensure a satisfactory appearance and in the interests of highway safety.
Condition : 20 - Before the development hereby permitted is first occupied or brought into use, a Delivery & Servicing Plan (including details of vehicle access and egress arrangements and times that servicing shall take place) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall accord with current guidance such as that issued by TfL and include measures required to ensure sufficient arrangements (physical as well as managerial) for the servicing, including refuse collection, of all aspects of the development, the timing of hours for deliveries by motor vehicles and a timetable for implementation. The development shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with the approved details and shall be maintained for the lifetime of the development, unless the prior written approval of the local planning authority is obtained to any variation.
Reason: In the interests of the safety of pedestrians and vehicles, to protect neighbours' living conditions and to support sustainable transport objectives.
Condition : 21 - Notwithstanding the submitted details and prior to occupation, full details (including manufacturer's specifications) of all cycle stands for the staff of, and visitors to, the development shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
The approved facilities shall be fully implemented and made available for use before any part of the development is first occupied and thereafter retained for use at all times without obstruction.
Reason: In order to support sustainable transport objectives.
Condition : 22 - Notwithstanding the details provided and prior to occupation, full details of the arrangements for the storing of waste and recycled materials (including details of how the placing of waste and recycled materials in a suitable location for collection would be undertaken and managed) have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with the approved details. 
Reason: In order to ensure adequate provision for waste and recycling.
Condition : 23 - Additional/unexpected contamination found during development
During the development:
The Local Planning Authority shall be notified immediately if unexpected contamination is discovered during the course of development. A competent person shall assess the contamination, where necessary, including soil and groundwater sampling and testing before any further part of the development that may be affected by the discovered contamination continues. 
A remediation method statement, prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person, shall be submitted in writing to the local planning authority for approval within one month of the discovery of such contamination. 
Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site or in proximity due to former land uses. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.
Supporting notes:
(i) Remediation work to remove or manage unexpected contamination shall be carried out in accordance with the approved remediation method statement for verification and validation before the development is first brought into use. 
(ii) In some instances, the local planning authority may require work on site to be ceased whilst the nature of unexpected contamination is investigated fully.
(iii) The Council requests that the remediation method statement or any site photos be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the local planning authority for approval.
Condition : 24 - Verification and validation of remedial work
Prior to the development is first brought into use:
The agreed scheme for remediation, including any amendments, shall be fully implemented. A verification report produced upon completion of the remediation by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person shall be submitted in writing to the local planning authority for approval, before the development is first brought into use or in accordance with a programme approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. 
Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.
Supporting notes:
(i) The verification (closure) report shall revisit the conceptual site model and provide evidence that each aspect of the remediation plan has been implemented correctly and successfully in accordance with current UK guidance and best practice. Where applicable, the report shall describe how any additional/unexpected contamination encountered during development has been managed in line with the revised remediation method statement. 
(ii) This report shall demonstrate that the development is suitable for its proposed use in terms of land quality.
(iii) The Council requests that the verification report or site photos be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval.
description: Erection of canopy encompassing three padel courts and the installation of two outdoor padel courts. Erection of two single storey shipping containers comprising of clubhouse, food and drink facility and toilet/changing facilities with associated landscaping and cycle parking.
